article_title: Connecting Emotional Intelligence with Academic Performance and Family Dynamics among Fresh Undergraduates in a Health Sciences University: Preliminary Findings.
citation: Falade Joshua, Adebayo Ezekiel Taiwo, Eegunranti Benjamin Adekunle, Fatusi Adesegun Olayiwola. (2025). Connecting Emotional Intelligence with Academic Performance and Family Dynamics among Fresh Undergraduates in a Health Sciences University: Preliminary Findings. Ethiopian Journal of Health Sciences 35(1). https://doi.org/10.4314/ejhs.v35i1.7
title: Wong and Law Emotional Intelligence Scale (WLEIS) with GHQ-12 screening in a fresh-undergraduate census
description: The study measured EI with the Wong and Law Emotional Intelligence Scale, "a widely used tool based on the ability model of EI" with four dimensions: self-emotional appraisal, others' emotional appraisal, regulation of emotion, and use of emotion. Respondents rated 16 statements on a 7-point scale, and those scoring 48 points or more (50%) were classified as above-average EI. Psychiatric morbidity was screened with the GHQ-12 using binary 0-0-1-1 scoring, a score of 3 or above indicating morbidity. The census approach surveyed fresh undergraduates from November 2023 to January 2024.
requirements: Self-administered questionnaire completion with informed consent; WLEIS validated in Nigeria with reported Cronbach's alpha = 0.92 in a pilot among 50 secondary school teachers
constraints: The article notes the self-reported nature of the data introduces potential for bias, and concerns about identification and stigma could have influenced responses
target_learners: fresh undergraduates in a health sciences university
target_learning_goals: emotional intelligence (self-emotional appraisal, others' emotional appraisal, regulation of emotion, use of emotion)
examples: A census of 560 of 580 fresh undergraduates (96.6% response rate) at UNIMED Ondo completed the questionnaires during routine medical screening
